items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: You see, Alan? Somebody must have told them... Then they wrote to me... I made that particular business to find that out for you.

ctx.x: Papa, how did those men know your name, those St. Louis fellas? How did they know your name? They learned it through me. Did...

You see, Alan? Somebody must have told them, or they must have found out who I was, or where they could define me. Then they wrote to me. Asked me to send them, them men. Send them three musicians. See? But they didn't come down here personally. No, no. No, no. They wrote to you. Then I asked them, forward the tickets and I'll send them in. And the tickets. Your tickets, your tickets, tickets off to St. Louis. I wasn't going to send them for that to get the tickets for that St. Louis. Sure. And the return ticket…
Did you teach them much when you went up there? Huh? Did you... Could you teach them much when you went up there by doing? No. No. No, I didn't.
